title: Coefficient comparisons: units, composition and purity
statement:
Work in the standing scheme setting of the smooth-purity chapter: $k$ is the algebraic closure in the global finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, $X,Y$ are separated finite-type $k$-schemes, and $f:X\to Y$ is a smooth separated $k$-morphism of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let $A\to B$ (and, in clause 2, $B\to C$) be unital maps of finite commutative rings killed by powers of $\ell$. Use the ordinary, uncompleted constant-coefficient pro-etale module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]; $\Dctf(T,R)$ denotes their bounded objects with intrinsically constructible cohomology [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf] and finite Tor amplitude [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude], meaning that some interval $[a,b]$ contains the cohomology of $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N$ for every degree-zero $R_T$-module sheaf $N$.

Use the scalar-extension functors and associators of [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor], the compact-support comparison $b_{A,B}(M):(Rf_{!,A}M)_B\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{!,B}(M_B)$ of [det-sp-reduction-direct-image], pinned as follows: for a compactification $f=pj$, take the coefficient exchange for $Rp_*$ (the adjunction mate of the coefficient/pullback balancing isomorphism), followed by the canonical coefficient identification for $j_!$, and the counit-characterized comparison $c_{A,B}(K):(f_A^!K)_B\xrightarrow{\sim}f_B^!(K_B)$ of [det-sp-reduction-exceptional]. Write $b=b_{A,B}$, and write $\eta_R,\varepsilon_R$ for the unit and counit of $Rf_{!,R}\dashv f_R^!$. The purity maps $\gamma_{f,R}$ use the diagonal/DNC orientation specified over general finite rings by [det-sp-finite-general-ring].

1. *Units.* For $M\in\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{proét}},A)$, in $\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{proét}},B)$,
   $$
   f_B^!\bigl(b(M)\bigr)\circ c_{A,B}(Rf_{!,A}M)\circ (\eta_A(M))_B=\eta_B(M_B).
   $$
2. *Composition.* For $A\to B\to C$ and $K\in\Dctf(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},A)$, the composite
   $(f_A^!K)_C\simeq((f_A^!K)_B)_C\xrightarrow{c_{A,B}(K)_C}(f_B^!K_B)_C
   \xrightarrow{c_{B,C}(K_B)}f_C^!((K_B)_C)\simeq f_C^!K_C$
   equals $c_{A,C}(K)$.
3. *Purity.* For $K\in\Dctf(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},A)$, in $\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{proét}},B)$,
   $$
   c_{A,B}(K)\circ (\gamma_{f,A}(K))_B=\gamma_{f,B}(K_B),
   $$
   the sources being identified by $(f_A^*K(d)[2d])_B\simeq f_B^*(K_B)(d)[2d]$.

proof.text: Set $P_R=Rf_{!,R}$, $G_R=f_R^!$, $T^W_{A,B}=-\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_W}B_W$ for $W=X,Y$, and $\omega_R=G_RR_Y$. The comparisons $b:T^YP_A\to P_BT^X$ and $c:T^XG_A\to G_BT^Y$ have the direction in the statement. Scalar extension preserves the finite-Tor constructible domains and the shifted Tate line by [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor]. Its monoidal identification $T(U\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}V)\cong TU\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}TV$ follows by applying [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] to the identity topos with structure-ring map $A_W\to B_W$. The pullback identification $T^Xf_A^*K\cong f_B^*T^YK$ is the balancing map for the two compositions of module pullbacks: $(f^{-1}K\otimes_A A_X)\otimes_A B_X\cong f^{-1}K\otimes_A B_X$. On flat K-flat representatives it multiplies the nested scalars; both triple composites multiply the same three scalars. These identifications are natural and respect tensor symmetry and shifts; balancing preserves degrees, and the tensor symmetry on a pair of degrees $r,s$ uses the same sign $(-1)^{rs}$ on either side. We use these fixed identifications below, including the natural associators $(U_B)_C\cong U_C$; no flatness of $B/A$ is used. The current direct-image comparison phrases bounded constructibility intrinsically. The equivalence of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin] identifies bounded constructible etale-origin objects with exactly those bounded intrinsically constructible pro-etale objects, for every finite commutative ring here. The finite-Tor condition is the same test against degree-zero module sheaves on the same pro-etale category. Thus all inputs used below satisfy the revised direct-image comparison's hypotheses, without identifying a condensed coefficient category with the ordinary one.

source.place: Conventions preceding clauses (1)-(3); tensor and pullback identifications made explicit

proof.text:
For clause 1 let $L=P_AM$. Transpose its left side under $P_B\dashv G_B$. Naturality of $\varepsilon_B$ first moves $G_B(b_M)$ to the outside. The defining equation for $c_L$ in [det-sp-reduction-exceptional] then gives the transpose
$$b_M\circ(\varepsilon_A(L))_B\circ b_{G_AL}^{-1}\circ P_B((\eta_A(M))_B).$$
Naturality of $b$ at $\eta_A(M):M\to G_AP_AM$ rewrites the last two factors as $(P_A\eta_A(M))_B\circ b_M^{-1}$. Thus this transpose is
$$b_M\circ\bigl(\varepsilon_A(P_AM)\circ P_A\eta_A(M)\bigr)_B\circ b_M^{-1}=1_{P_BM_B},$$
by the triangle identity of the $A$-adjunction. This is the transpose of $\eta_B(M_B)$, so injectivity of the adjunction Hom bijection proves clause 1. The only identities used besides the cited counit equation and naturality of $b$ are the naturality and triangle axioms of the displayed adjunctions.

For clause 2 put $q=c_{B,C}(K_B)\circ(c_{A,B}(K))_C$, inserting the source and target associators of Step 1. Its transpose under $P_C\dashv G_C$ is
$$\begin{aligned}
\varepsilon_C(K_C)P_C(q)
&=(\varepsilon_B(K_B))_C\,b_{B,C}(G_BK_B)^{-1}\,P_C((c_{A,B}(K))_C)\\
&=\bigl(\varepsilon_B(K_B)P_B(c_{A,B}(K))\bigr)_C\,b_{B,C}((G_AK)_B)^{-1}\\
&=(\varepsilon_A(K))_C\,(b_{A,B}(G_AK)^{-1})_C\,b_{B,C}((G_AK)_B)^{-1}\\
&=(\varepsilon_A(K))_C\,b_{A,C}(G_AK)^{-1}.
\end{aligned}$$
The first and third equalities are the defining counit equations for $c_{B,C}$ and $c_{A,B}$. The second is naturality of $b_{B,C}$ at $c_{A,B}(K)$. The last is exactly the coefficient cocycle in [det-sp-reduction-direct-image]; naturality of the scalar associator puts its two factors in the indicated order. This last expression is the transpose of $c_{A,C}(K)$. Equality of transposes proves clause 2, for every input $K$ in its stated domain.

source.place: Proof (2), expanded naturality and inverse-cocycle calculation

proof.text:
We first justify the projection compatibility used in the tensor-map part of clause 3. Fix one compactification $f=pj$ used by $b$ in [det-sp-reduction-direct-image]. For its proper part use [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence] on the following square of ringed topoi: the horizontal scheme maps are $p$ over $A$ and $p$ over $B$, and the two vertical morphisms are identity topoi equipped with the maps $A_Y\to B_Y$ and $A_{\bar X}\to B_{\bar X}$. The ringed square commutes because inverse image sends the constant coefficient map to the same coefficient map on $\bar X$. Its vertical derived pullbacks are precisely $T^Y,T^{\bar X}$; its exchange is the counit-defined proper coefficient comparison used to construct $b$. The cited theorem requires a commutative ringed square, not a cartesian square, and has no flatness assumption. It therefore identifies the two routes through the proper projection map and coefficient exchange. The open part is the canonical projection isomorphism of [lem-cbc-extension-zero-projection-formula]. Its compatibility with coefficient change can be checked on flat K-flat representatives: both orders use the balanced map that extends a section by zero, tensors its coefficient with the other factor, and multiplies the two $B$-scalars. On $U$ the maps are the identical balancing map; on the complement their source and target are zero. Thus this is an equality of the underived natural module maps in each bidegree and hence of their total-complex maps, not detection of equality of arbitrary derived maps on an open cover. Pasting the proper and open squares gives
$$b_{M\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}f_A^*K}\circ(\operatorname{PF}_{A;M,K})_B
=\operatorname{PF}_{B;M_B,K_B}\circ(b_M\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}1_{K_B}),$$
under the monoidal and pullback identifications of Step 1. Here $\operatorname{PF}_R$ is the canonical proper projection followed by the open projection for this compactification. This is valid in particular for $M=\omega_A$; all $b$ components in this instance are on finite-Tor constructible inputs.

source.place: Proof (3), Tensor map: projection formula commutes with coefficients; proper part is Stacks Tag 0E48 (remark-compatible-with-diagram), open part Tag 0GL1 (lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor)

proof.text:
The projection maps used next are invertible on the required domain for every finite coefficient ring $R$ in the statement. The object $K$ has bounded intrinsically constructible cohomology by its stated $\Dctf$ hypothesis, while [det-sp-finite-general-ring] identifies $\omega_R$ with the shifted Tate line $R_X(d)[2d]$, which is bounded with intrinsically constructible cohomology (locally free of rank one, placed in degree $-2d$). The compactification $f=pj$ fixed in Step 4 has all three schemes separated of finite type over $k$, and $R$ is finite and $\ell$-primary. Hence [lem-sp-finite-ring-compact-support-projection], applied with $M=\omega_R$, says that the compact-support projection map $\operatorname{PF}_{R;\omega_R,K}$ of Step 4 (the canonical proper projection followed by the open projection isomorphism) is an isomorphism. This uses neither a DVR presentation of $R$ nor a projection theorem for arbitrary nonclassical pro-etale complexes.

Let $U_R(K)=f_R^*K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}\omega_R$. Write $h_{R,K}:U_R(K)\to G_RK$ for the canonical tensor map occurring in [det-sp-finite-general-ring]. Explicitly its transpose is
$$t_{R,K}:P_RU_R(K)\xrightarrow{P_R(\sigma)}P_R(\omega_R\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}f_R^*K)\xrightarrow{\operatorname{PF}_{R;\omega_R,K}^{-1}}P_R\omega_R\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}K\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_R(R_Y)\otimes1}K.$$
The final coefficient-unit isomorphism is understood. This gives the precise meaning of the canonical tensor map, with the same symmetry convention at both coefficient rings.

source.place: Proof (3), Tensor map: projection inverses for arbitrary finite rings via the current finite comparison unit and Stacks Tag 0F0G; explicit counit transpose

proof.text:
Let $\delta=c_{A,B}(A_Y): (\omega_A)_B\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_B$, identifying $(A_Y)_B=B_Y$. Let $\rho_K:(U_A(K))_B\to U_B(K_B)$ be the monoidal/pullback identification of Step 1 followed by $1\otimes\delta$. Step 4, now inverted, and naturality of the projection map in its first variable identify the projection portion of $t_{B,K_B}P_B(\rho_K)$ with the scalar extension of the projection portion of $t_{A,K}$, followed by $b_{U_A(K)}^{-1}$. The remaining counit portion is exactly
$$\varepsilon_B(B_Y)P_B(\delta)=(\varepsilon_A(A_Y))_B\,b_{\omega_A}^{-1}$$
from [det-sp-reduction-exceptional]. Consequently
$$t_{B,K_B}P_B(\rho_K)=(t_{A,K})_B\,b_{U_A(K)}^{-1}.$$
For completeness, the transpose of $c_{A,B}(K)(h_{A,K})_B$ is, by the same defining identity and naturality of $b$ at $h_{A,K}$,
$$\begin{aligned}
\varepsilon_B(K_B)P_B(c_{A,B}(K))P_B((h_{A,K})_B)
&=(\varepsilon_A(K))_B\,b_{G_AK}^{-1}\,P_B((h_{A,K})_B)\\
&=(\varepsilon_A(K)P_A(h_{A,K}))_B\,b_{U_A(K)}^{-1}\\
&=(t_{A,K})_B\,b_{U_A(K)}^{-1}.
\end{aligned}$$
The transpose of $h_{B,K_B}\rho_K$ is the same by the preceding equation. Injectivity of transposition proves
$$c_{A,B}(K)(h_{A,K})_B=h_{B,K_B}\rho_K.$$
This establishes coefficient compatibility of the tensor maps before choosing an orientation.

source.place: Proof (3), Tensor map: counit compatibility and equality of explicit transposes

proof.text:
To compare orientations for this particular $A\to B$, choose a single $n\geq1$ with $\ell^nA=\ell^nB=0$, and put $R=\mathbf Z/\ell^n$. The unital ring map $A\to B$ makes $R\to A\to B$ a chain. Let $o_R:R_X(d)[2d]\to\omega_R$ be the inverse of the prime-power diagonal/DNC orientation. Clauses 1 and 2 of [det-sp-finite-general-ring] say that the inverse diagonal/DNC orientations over $A,B$ are
$$o_A=c_{R,A}(R_Y)(o_R)_A,\qquad o_B=c_{R,B}(R_Y)(o_R)_B.$$
All source twists are identified by the free-rank-one clause of [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor], valid even for a nonflat coefficient map. Clause 2 of the present item, already proved in Step 3, applied to $R\to A\to B$ at $R_Y$, gives the explicit equality
$$\delta\,(o_A)_B
=c_{A,B}(A_Y)(c_{R,A}(R_Y))_B(o_R)_B
=c_{R,B}(R_Y)(o_R)_B=o_B.$$
We use the stated common-origin formula and its agreement with the diagonal construction; we do not assume that arbitrary isomorphisms of derived objects glue or that an unspecified DNC comparison is uniquely determined by a fibre. The purity maps $\gamma_{f,A},\gamma_{f,B}$ of the statement may be computed with this common exponent $n$ by the exponent-independence assertion of clause 3 of [det-sp-finite-general-ring].

source.place: Proof (3), Orientation: explicit common-prime-power construction; current blueprint sk-thm-smooth-purity-general-ring clauses (1)-(2)

proof.text:
By the displayed construction in [det-sp-finite-general-ring], $\gamma_{f,A}(K)=h_{A,K}\circ(1\otimes o_A)$ after the canonical twist reassociation, and similarly over $B$. Substitute the tensor-map equality of Step 6 and then $\delta(o_A)_B=o_B$ from Step 7. Functoriality of tensor gives
$$\begin{aligned}
c_{A,B}(K)(\gamma_{f,A}(K))_B
&=h_{B,K_B}\rho_K(1\otimes o_A)_B\\
&=h_{B,K_B}(1\otimes o_B)=\gamma_{f,B}(K_B).
\end{aligned}$$
The source identification is precisely $(f_A^*K(d)[2d])_B\cong f_B^*(K_B)(d)[2d]$ from Step 1. This proves clause 3. Together with Steps 2 and 3 it proves all three assertions.
